articles.title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound: A Transformative Tool for Intracranial Ablation, Drug Delivery, and Neuromodulation
articles.content: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) is an emerging neuromodulation and therapeutic technology offering noninvasive, submillimeter precision for targeting deep brain structures. Unlike transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial electric stimulation (tES), which are limited by depth-focality tradeoffs, or deep brain stimulation (DBS), which is invasive and costly, tFUS enables precise modulation with minimal risk. Its applications include ablation for movement and psychiatric disorders, blood-brain barrier opening (BBBO) for drug delivery in neuro-oncology and neurodegeneration, and neuromodulation for circuit-based interventions in addiction, mood/anxiety disorders, and chronic pain. Advances in phased-array transducers, holographic focusing, and real-time imaging continue to refine its accuracy and safety. Ongoing research explores closed-loop systems and wearable devices to expand clinical accessibility. This review outlines the physics, current applications, and future directions of tFUS, positioning it as a transformative tool in personalized neuromodulation and neurotherapeutics.

articles.title: Brainstem premotor circuits transform dental sensory input into coordinated jaw opening
articles.content: Protective actions require the rapid transformation of damage into coordinated activity of motor pools, yet the brainstem circuits implementing this operation remain poorly defined. Here, we use the tooth-trigeminal system to identify molecularly specified pathways linking intradental sensory input to opposing jaw motor pools. Optogenetic activation of tooth-associated sensory afferents evoked rapid, stimulus-locked jaw-opening. Intradental afferents formed functional monosynaptic connections with Pdyn+ neurons in the 5Sol transition zone and Calb2+ neurons in the 5Tr transition zone, identifying these regions as sensory-recipient premotor interfaces. Predominantly excitatory Pdyn+ 5Sol neurons provided monosynaptic input to anterior digastric motor neurons, whereas predominantly inhibitory Calb2+ 5Tr neurons provided bilateral monosynaptic input to masseter motor neurons. Activation of Pdyn+ 5Sol neurons was sufficient to evoke jaw opening. Together, these findings define complementary brainstem pathways positioned to couple jaw-opening drive with inhibition of antagonistic jaw-closing output, revealing a withdrawal-like sensorimotor computation adapted to cranial biomechanics.
articles.author: Liu, L.-Y., Lee, H., Wagner, N., Hunter, K., Lee, E., Constantinescu, B. S. C., Dakhilalla, L., Chang, A., Duan, B., Emrick, J.

articles.title: Long-Term Reconfiguration of Dynamic Polarization and Action Potential Initiation in Purkinje Cell Axons
articles.content: Ramon y Cajal seminally predicted ''the law of dynamic polarization of the neuron'': synaptic inputs are integrated in the dendrites and soma, which are transformed into action potentials (APs) at the axon initial segment, faithfully propagating to the axon terminal for outputs toward target neurons. However, the exceedingly small size of axons and terminals in central neurons has hindered complete validation of this unidirectional signaling scheme. Here, using cutting-edge genetically-encoded fluorescent voltage imaging, complemented by tour-de-force axonal patch-clamp recordings, I show that the traditional one-way neuronal computation exhibits dynamic, activity-dependent long-term plasticity. In cerebellar Purkinje cells, AP firing, typically initiating near the soma, drastically shifts toward various sites of initiation in axons for more than two days, following the chemical induction of learning-related dendritic long-term postsynaptic plasticity. The dynamic shift of AP initiation is accompanied by enhanced GABAA receptor activity and increased membrane excitability in the axon terminals. Thus, dendritic postsynaptic plasticity induces sustained axonal plasticity, giving rise to the emergence of local input-output elements at multiple terminals, which occasionally function as partially independent computation units. Together, the present study reveals an unprecedented dynamic modulation of neuronal processing, revolutionizing neuronal circuit computation.
articles.author: Kawaguchi, S.-y.

articles.title: Valine Engages a Prefrontal mGluR5 Allosteric Site to Preserve Social Behavior
articles.content: Branched-chain amino acid metabolism is linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, but whether a defined amino acid directly modulates cortical receptor signaling to control behavior is unknown. Here, we show that valine is uniquely required for sociability through medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) circuitry. Partial dietary valine restriction, but not comparable leucine or isoleucine restriction, or mPFC-restricted acceleration of BCAA catabolism through Bckdk loss, disrupts social interaction, and local valine supplementation rescues behavior. LiP-SMap, surface plasmon resonance, cryo-EM, and mutagenesis identify metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) as a direct valine target and reveal a valine-selective allosteric pocket distinct from the glutamate site. Valine is signaling-biased: it drives {beta}-arrestin-linked output yet has little standalone Gq efficacy, instead potentiating glutamate-evoked mGluR5 signaling to recruit endocannabinoid/CB1 feedback, gate inhibitory transmission, and preserve mPFC-dependent social behavior. Together, these findings identify valine as a diet-derived allosteric ligand that links amino acid availability to cortical circuit control of social behavior.
articles.author: Shan, X., Zhu, T., Wang, Y., Shi, T.-T., Yang, X., Wang, S., Zhang, X., Zhou, W., Zhou, Z.-Y., Geng, H.-R., Yan, J., Lv, H., Yan, Y., Guo, Y., Shi, L., Zhang, L., Hu, K., Wang, D., Yu, Y., Mei, B., Zhang, Q., Sun, H., Wang, X., Qu, Q., Zhao, J.-Y., Li, W.-G., Li, F.

articles.title: Economic hardship mediates differences in brain network dynamics associated with family history of substance use disorder in a sex-specific manner
articles.content: Family history of substance use disorder (SUD) is associated with brain differences before substance exposure, but the pathways linking familial risk to brain function may differ by sex. Using baseline data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, we tested whether environmental adversity mediates previously observed sex-specific associations between family history of SUD and transition energy, a network control theory-derived measure of the energetic cost of transitioning between brain activity states. We derived three environmental dimensions - economic hardship, family-school neglect, and parental mental illness - and fit sex-stratified mediation models at global, network, and regional scales. Environmental mediation was significant in females and was driven primarily by economic hardship, which mediated higher transition energy across default mode, visual, ventral attention, and somatomotor networks, with widespread positive regional effects. In males, mediation was weaker and more heterogeneous, with more negative transition-energy patterns that were less explained by the measured environmental pathways. In an exploratory extension, state policy environments associated with smaller FH+ versus FH- economic-hardship gaps were projected to partially attenuate FH-related transition energy gaps, especially in females. These findings suggest that familial SUD risk is embedded in brain dynamics through sex-distinct pathways, with economic hardship representing a potentially modifiable pathway linking familial risk to large-scale brain function in early adolescence.
articles.author: Schilling, L. S., Hedo, M., Jamison, K., Gillies, C., Radanovic, A., Hedo, M., Kuceyeski, A.

articles.title: Structural topology shapes regional roles in neuronal avalanche initiation and termination
articles.content: Whole-brain dynamics unfold as fast, discrete, transient events known as, neuronal avalanches, whose propagation is constrained by the connectome, that is, the large-scale scaffolding of structural connections wiring the brain. However, the role of the connectome in determining the topographies of the start and end of these transient cascades remains unclear. Leveraging resting-state Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) tractography across 42 healthy individuals, we examined whether the structural architecture of white matter tracts dictates the spatial origins and the end of cortical avalanches. We found that the probability of triggering and finishing an avalanche is strongly related to the structural nodal strength, showing a positive correlation that is highly robust to non-parametric spatial permutation testing and bootstrapping. This structure-function coupling is highly stable and robust across different activation thresholds, demonstrating that the choice of avalanche extraction threshold does not drive or alter our main findings. Collectively, our results suggest that structural properties determine a region's propensity to initiate and terminate neuronal avalanches.
articles.author: De luca, M., Demuru, M., Troisi Lopez, E., Gallo, E., Cafaro, G., Duma, G. M., Depannemaecker, D., Casagrande, G., Quarantelli, M., Granata, C., Sorrentino, G., Sorrentino, P., Angiolelli, M.

articles.title: Unilateral gene expression via maternally controlled zygotic recombination in Drosophila
articles.content: Structural and functional asymmetries are ubiquitous in bilaterians, but tools for unilateral genetic access have been lacking, a methodological gap that has limited mechanistic dissections of lateralized cellular functions. We developed the Maternally Controlled Zygotic Recombination (MCZR) system to overcome this limitation in Drosophila, co-opting the regulatory machinery of the maternal-to-zygotic transition to enable somatic recombination during early embryonic development. Targeting recombinase activity to this early window generates large somatic mosaics that frequently split across the anatomical midline. In conjunction with cell type-specific driver lines, this approach provides a reliable, scalable, and user-friendly platform for unilateral transgene expression. In proof-of-concept experiments, we apply our tool to the question of locomotor control, illustrating how MCZR can be used to unilaterally manipulate or monitor a cell type of interest. Overall, the MCZR system unlocks previously inaccessible experimental avenues across neuroscience, cell biology, and developmental biology.
articles.author: Currier, T. A., Tadres, D., Troper, J. E., Wang, Y., Clandinin, T. R.

articles.title: Prior visual context accelerates the emergence of object representations
articles.content: Our knowledge about how the world is structured allows for predictions about what objects we might see next. Visual context is known to impact the perception of subsequent objects, but we do not know what context does to the mental representation of those objects. Using MEG, we tested how a scene context changes the neural representation of visual objects, and whether the context simply enhances expected object representations, or if it acts to reorganise the temporal trajectory of object information in the brain. Using temporal generalisation decoding, we show that multiple dimensions of semantic information are shifted up to 200 ms earlier when the object and the prior context are congruent, and this temporally-shifted decoding was related to behavioural object recognition speed. This suggests that prior context can warp the temporal trajectory through which object representations are accessed and accelerate the emergence of semantic object representations in the mind.
articles.author: Clarke, A., Gu, Y., Krugliak, A.

articles.title: Delayed maturation of hippocampal trisynaptic circuitry underlies the protracted development of episodic-like memory
articles.content: The ability to form high-resolution episodic memories emerges relatively late in development, but the circuit mechanisms underlying this transition are unknown. CA1 receives entorhinal input through a direct monosynaptic pathway and an indirect trisynaptic pathway via the dentate gyrus and CA3. In mice, CA3[->]CA1 innervation matured later than MEC[->]CA1 innervation, with pronounced maturation between P20 and P24. Trisynaptic pathway maturation was necessary for high-resolution memory and was shaped by neuronal activity and early-life experience. Mechanistically, trisynaptic activity promoted perineuronal net assembly around downstream parvalbumin-expressing interneurons, facilitating their maturation and subsequent recruitment during learning to constrain CA1 encoding ensembles. Thus, activity-dependent maturation of trisynaptic circuitry provides a unified circuit and cellular account of a sensitive period for the emergence of episodic-like memory.
articles.author: McKenzie, C., Ramsaran, A. I., Saderi, M., Haar, S., Josselyn, S. A., Frankland, P. W.

articles.title: Kilohertz electrical stimulation drives widespread neuronal activation and temporal interference imposes focal rhythmic modulation
articles.content: Temporal interference (TI) stimulation has attracted attention as a non-invasive approach that can target deep brain structures through interacting kilohertz-frequency electric fields. Its basic premise is that TI stimulation evokes neuronal responses through low-frequency amplitude modulation (AM), while the underlying kilohertz-frequency stimulation is ineffective to induce activity, the latter of which has not been tested rigorously at the cellular level. Here, we combined two-photon imaging in mouse models with immunohistochemistry and computational modeling to characterize spatiotemporal patterns of neuronal responses during TI stimulation. We found that kilohertz-frequency stimulation was sufficient to evoke activity without AM. In contrast, AM organized neuronal activity into rhythmic responses at AM frequency, with the strongest entrainment near the center of interference. Thus, kilohertz-frequency stimulation can drive widespread neuronal activation, upon which TI imposes focal rhythmic modulation. Our results provide a framework for refining TI stimulation and highlight the potential of kilohertz-frequency stimulation for brain stimulation.
articles.author: Yoshimoto, R., Stern, M. A., Eggers, T., Acerbo, E., Laxpati, N. G., Berglund, K., Gutekunst, C.-A.

articles.title: Sex-dependent endocannabinoid adaptations in supraspinal pain modulatory circuits after peripheral nerve injury
articles.content: Peripheral nerve injury produces persistent pain-related behaviours that differ between sexes, but whether chronic neuropathic pain is accompanied by sex-dependent alterations in endocannabinoid signalling across pain-modulatory circuits remains unclear. We quantified endocannabinoids and related N-acylethanolamines and expression of cannabinoid receptors and metabolic enzymes across supraspinal and spinal regions 100 days after spared nerve injury (SNI) in male and female rats. SNI increased 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) in the prefrontal cortex and 2-AG in the rostral ventromedial medulla in males, with exploratory associations between these measures and reduced pain-related hypersensitivity. In females, SNI increased monoacylglycerol lipase expression in the periaqueductal grey. Additional sex- and hemisphere-dependent differences in ECS components were observed in limbic regions,whereas no significant injury-related changes were detected in spinal cord or plasma. These findings identify regionally distinct ECS alterations during established neuropathic pain and suggest that chronic nerve injury is associated with different patterns of supraspinal ECS plasticity in males and females.
articles.author: Boullon, L., Finn, D. P., Llorente-Berzal, A.

articles.title: Agreement and longitudinal repeatability of established brain volumetry pipelines across healthy controls, multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer's disease
articles.content: IntroductionBrain volume estimates are increasingly used as longitudinal endpoints in neuroimaging studies and clinical trials, but outputs from different segmentation pipelines may not be interchangeable. In this study, we performed a version-specific comparison of six established brain segmentation pipelines across healthy controls (HC; n = 20), people with multiple sclerosis (MS; n = 19), and people with Alzheimer's disease (AD; n = 50).MethodsFreeSurfer v6, FreeSurfer v7.2, SAMSEG, FastSurfer v1, SIENAX/SIENA-XL, and CAT12 were evaluated. The primary aims were to quantify systematic offsets and inter-pipeline agreement in normalized baseline volume estimates, assess within-pipeline repeatability and longitudinal change-from-baseline concordance, and determine whether longitudinal processing reduced variability relative to cross-sectional processing. Gray matter, white matter, hippocampus, and thalamus were selected and normalized to intracranial volume. Agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients, while longitudinal change was evaluated using mixed-effects models and repeatability metrics.ResultsBaseline volume estimates differed significantly across pipelines in 11 of 12 cohort-by-tissue comparisons (FDR-adjusted p < 0.001), with the largest pipeline-dependent offsets observed for grey matter, hippocampus, and thalamus. Inter-pipeline agreement was generally strong for white matter and lower for gray matter and subcortical structures (hippocampus and thalamus), particularly in pathological cohorts. Change-from-baseline models showed no significant Pipeline × Timepoint interactions after FDR correction, indicating broadly parallel longitudinal trajectories across pipelines after baseline normalization. However, significant pipeline main effects persisted in selected tissues, especially in AD and subcortical regions, indicating residual differences in the magnitude of estimated change. Longitudinal processing reduced within-subject variability in selected settings, particularly for FreeSurfer-derived hippocampal and thalamic estimates, but did not uniformly improve stability across all pipelines or tissues.DiscussionTogether, these findings show that systematic offset, absolute agreement, longitudinal change magnitude, and short-interval repeatability represent distinct properties of volumetric pipelines and vary by tissue, cohort, and processing mode. Longitudinal processing reduced variability but not uniformly, highlighting pipeline- and tissue-dependent differences relevant to the interpretation of longitudinal volumetric measurements.
